findings.summary: Regular monitoring service health checks targeting web server.
findings.reasoning: Traffic originates from the designated monitoring host (10.0.0.5) performing regular health checks, dismiss as benign look-alike.

findings.summary: Brute force attack targeting SSH root account from external IP.
findings.reasoning: Multiple consecutive failed password attempts for the root user from an external IP address (203.0.113.228).

findings.summary: External port scanning against SSH server.
findings.reasoning: Sequential TCP port scanning activity observed from external IPs targeting ssh-srv.

findings.summary: Successful SSH brute force followed by privilege escalation via sudo.
findings.reasoning: External IP 203.0.113.13 brute-forced the 'deploy' account, successfully logged in, and escalated privileges to root via sudo.

findings.summary: Suspicious large outbound data transfer to external IP on non-standard port 4444.
findings.reasoning: High volume outbound transfer (150MB) from ssh-srv to external IP 198.51.100.200 on port 4444, indicating potential data exfiltration or reverse shell.

findings.summary: Internal administrative or automated multi-user login sessions showing normal login patterns.
findings.reasoning: Internal IPs performing successful logins after minor authentication retries or concurrent usage. Normal internal management activity, dismiss as benign look-alikes.

findings.summary: Password spraying attack across multiple internal user accounts.
findings.reasoning: External IP 203.0.113.32 systematically attempts login against a wide range of user accounts in a short timeframe.

findings.summary: Web request containing escaped apostrophe (benign search query).
findings.reasoning: Query parameter contains O'Brien, standard user input, dismiss as benign look-alike.

findings.summary: SQL injection attempts using sqlmap tool against web server.
findings.reasoning: Web logs show explicit SQL injection payloads and user-agent string identifying the sqlmap scanner.

findings.summary: Legitimate administrative sudo session by sysadmin.
findings.reasoning: The inventory designates 'sysadmin' as the admin user executing administrative commands during working hours, dismiss as benign.

findings.summary: Path traversal attack targeting web server files endpoint.
findings.reasoning: Repeated GET requests attempting directory traversal via ../../etc/passwd.

findings.summary: Scheduled nightly backup traffic to backup server.
findings.reasoning: Outbound connection from 10.0.0.10 to the designated backup server 192.0.2.10 on port 443, matching inventory expectations, dismiss as benign.

incidents.title: Compromise of SSH Server via Credential Brute Force and Subsequent Data Exfiltration

kill_chain.description: External port scanning against the SSH server.
SSH brute force attempts against root user.
Successful SSH login using compromised credentials followed by sudo privilege escalation.
Large outbound data transfer to external command and control IP.

incidents.rationale: An external IP performed port scanning and brute-forced SSH accounts, successfully gained access to the deploy user, escalated privileges to root, and exfiltrated data to an external address.

incidents.title: Credential Spraying Campaign Against SSH Server

kill_chain.description: Password spraying attack across multiple valid accounts.

incidents.rationale: External IP 203.0.113.32 systematically attempted authentications against multiple users on the SSH server.

incidents.title: Web Application Attack Campaign (SQL Injection and Path Traversal)

kill_chain.description: Automated SQL injection scanning and exploitation attempts.
Path traversal attempts targeting system files.

incidents.rationale: External IPs targeted the web server with automated SQL injection payloads and directory traversal requests.

plans.executive_summary: The SSH server (ssh-srv) was compromised via brute-force authentication, leading to unauthorized privilege escalation and subsequent data exfiltration to an external IP.

immediate_actions.action: Block malicious attacker IP at firewall

investigation_steps: Review SSH authentication logs for any other successful logins from 203.0.113.13 or 203.0.113.228.
Perform forensic analysis on ssh-srv to inspect modified binaries, cron jobs, and active network connections.
Inspect the contents of the outbound data transfer to 198.51.100.200.
prevention: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all SSH access.
Disable password-based authentication and mandate SSH keys.
Implement egress filtering to block unauthorized outbound connections on non-standard ports.

plans.executive_summary: A password spraying attack was detected targeting multiple user accounts on the SSH server from an external IP.
investigation_steps: Check authentication logs for any successful logins originating from 203.0.113.32.
Review account activity for all users targeted in the spray.
prevention: Implement account lockout policies or rate limiting for failed authentication attempts.
Deploy fail2ban or similar intrusion prevention tools.

plans.executive_summary: The web server (web-srv) was targeted with SQL injection and path traversal attempts by external scanning sources.
investigation_steps: Analyze web server access logs for any evidence of successful data extraction via SQL injection.
Review application error logs and file access permissions.
prevention: Ensure parameterized queries and input sanitization are enforced across all web applications.
Deploy a Web Application Firewall (WAF) to detect and block common attack patterns.
